name: Hofkirche Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: Innsbruck's Court Church fascinates as the 'Black Men Church' with Emperor Maximilian I's monumental cenotaph and 28 larger-than-life bronze statues.
preis: Adults €9.00, concessions €7.00, youth under 19 free (free with Innsbruck Card)
beschreibung:
Overview

The gothic Court Church in Innsbruck (Hofkirche)—reverently known in local dialect as the "Schwarzmander-Kirche" (Church of the Black Men)—ranks among Europe's most significant sacred art monuments. Situated at the edge of Innsbruck's historic old town adjacent to the Tyrolean Folk Art Museum, the three-aisled hall church houses the world-famous cenotaph of Emperor Maximilian I. Encircled by 28 larger-than-life bronze statues depicting historical and mythological ancestral figures, the monument represents a Renaissance masterwork of continental stature that has inspired awe for centuries. Conceived as an imperial mausoleum, this sacred landmark magnetically attracts art historians, scholars, and travelers from around the globe.

Route & Requirements

Emperor Ferdinand I commissioned the construction of the Court Church between 1553 and 1563 to fulfill the testament of his grandfather Maximilian I. At the center of the nave rises the grand empty tomb crafted from black marble, crowned by the bronze kneeling figure of the praying Emperor. The cenotaph is adorned with 24 exquisitely carved Carrara marble reliefs illustrating key milestones of Maximilian's life. Flanking the monument stand the legendary 28 bronze figures ("Black Men"), including King Arthur, Theodoric the Great, and Duke Rudolf IV, cast by prominent master sculptors such as Peter Vischer and Stefan Godl. The sculptural mastery of the bronze statues and the delicate carving of the choir screens reflect the transition from late Gothic to Renaissance styles. A staircase ascends to the Silver Chapel, containing a silver embossed Marian altar and the tombs of Archduke Ferdinand II and Philippine Welser. Another treasure is the historic swallow's nest pipe organ built by Jörg Ebert in 1558—one of the world's most prized Renaissance instruments.

Visit & Arrival

The Court Church is open Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 17:00, and Sundays and public holidays from 12:30 to 17:00. Admission: adults €9.00, reduced €7.00, under 19 free (combined ticket with the Tyrolean Folk Art Museum; free with the Innsbruck Card). Reaching the church: a five-minute walk from Central Station; tram and bus stop at Museumsstraße. Parking is available at the nearby Landesgarage or Altstadtgarage.

Tips

The church interior is wheelchair accessible via the main portal (the Silver Chapel is accessible by stairs only). Whenever possible, attend an organ recital on the 460-year-old Ebert organ. Tyrolean freedom fighter Andreas Hofer also rests here within a marble tomb. Pair your visit with the adjoining Tyrolean Folk Art Museum to view traditional wood-paneled parlors and alpine religious folk art.
